minutes.headline: Board declared a dog dangerous (4-1) and ordered muzzle, insurance and ID; also backed a nighttime truck ban letter.
minutes.summary: Most of the meeting was the continued dangerous dog hearing after a bite at a private beach. The board found the dog dangerous and ordered restraint, insurance and identification. It also appointed a personnel committee member, supported a nighttime heavy-truck exclusion letter, discussed a tri-centennial committee, reinstating liaisons, and the TC Passios design committee charge and missing minutes, and amended a remote participation policy.

public_comment.topic: Capital planning at-large seat has been advertised for ten days; encouraged public to apply.
Opposed holding a dog responsible for protecting its owner, general comments on dangerous dogs.
Mr. Pacios said past liaisons had drawn pushback from boards for impeding meetings and imposing on autonomy.
Mr. Allison said the liaison to planning board spoke as a citizen and recommended liaisons be observers who answer questions.

Town meeting funding will eventually be needed to celebrate the anniversary.

what_happened.line: The Select Board voted 4-1 to designate a dog dangerous after a bite at a private beach, ending a continued hearing.
The board then voted 5-0 to order a muzzle and restraint off premises, proof of insurance, and identification information for the dog.
Town counsel is to draft a written determination for board review; the owner then has 10 days to appeal.
The board voted 5-0 to accept a letter asking MassDOT for a nighttime heavy-vehicle restriction on four town roads.
The board amended its remote participation policy to add caring for an ill person as a permissible reason, and appointed a personnel committee member.

why_it_matters: The dog orders set the legal conditions the owner must meet, and the written determination starts the appeal period.
The truck letter is only a request to the state; any restriction depends on MassDOT, and a civil fine for violating a truck exclusion sign was described as small.
A tri-centennial committee could bring a funding request to a future Town Meeting vote.
watch_next: Ms. Adams' draft concept and motion wording for a tri-centennial committee, due at next week's meeting.
The written determination from town counsel on the dangerous dog, and the owner's 10-day appeal window after service.

reconciliation.what: Our minutes against the minutes the town published. caption_error = the same fact the captions rendered badly, resolved by the official reading shown beside the as-heard one; discrepancy = a substantive difference, flagged and not resolved. Neither record is treated as the referee.
reconciliation.summary: The records agree on the dog designation (4-1), the insurance amount, the warrants and the appeal period, with several names and one cents figure misheard in ours. Ours records three votes (muzzle/restraint condition, MassDOT letter, remote participation policy) plus the $25 fine, workshops and the Passios charge decision, which the official minutes do not mention, so a person should check whether those were omitted.
